name: de.echocall/echocall
title: EchoCall
description: Run EchoCall AI phone and chat agents from ChatGPT or Claude: calls, agents, knowledge and numbers.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description:
List voice agents

Returns the voice agents visible to the key, one page at a time, with a real total from a separate count query. An ordinary account key sees only its own agents; a reseller key sees every agent belonging to that reseller and can narrow the result to one customer with `userId`. Each item is the list form of an agent: no prompt, no model settings and no privacy settings, so fetch the individual agent when you need those. Note that the `status` query parameter is read but never applied, so passing it does not filter anything at present.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

status.description: Currently ignored. The handler parses this value but does not filter on it, so the response is the same whether or not it is sent.

userId.description: Reseller keys only: restrict the result to a single customer account. The key must be a reseller key and the account must be one of that reseller customers, otherwise the request is rejected with 403. Ignored for ordinary account keys, which always see only their own records.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description:
Create a voice agent

Creates a voice agent and provisions it in the voice engine in the same request, so the agent is ready to take calls as soon as the call succeeds. Only `name` and `language` are required; every other field falls back to a platform default, and `language` is normalised to a two-letter code, so a value like "german" is stored as `de`. The response is a short acknowledgement rather than the full agent, so read the agent back if you need the stored configuration. The new agent is created with status `active` and is owned by the account behind the key, or by the reseller for a reseller key.

name.description: The unique identifier name for your voice agent. Shown in the EchoCall dashboard.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., "en", "de"). This determines the base model and pronunciation rules.

supportedLanguages.description: All supported languages as ISO-639-1 codes. First element = primary language. E.g. ["de", "en", "fr"].

systemPrompt.description: Instructions that define the agent's personality, knowledge, and behavior. Use clear, concise commands.

firstMessage.description: The very first sentence the agent speaks when a call/chat begins. Supports SSML-like cues.

voiceId.description: The unique ID of the EchoCall voice to be used for speech synthesis.

temperature.description: Controls randomness. 0 is deterministic/focused, 100 is highly creative/varied.

llmModel.description: The advanced LLM "brain" powering the agent. Options: EchoCall-Voice, EchoCall-Smart.

maxTokens.description: Upper limit on the number of tokens the agent can generate per response.

ttsModel.description: Text-to-speech model. Leave unset for automatic selection based on `language`. `echocall-flash`: fast, multilingual (recommended default). `echocall-flash-lite`: fastest, English only. `echocall-ultra`: most expressive/natural, supports emotional audio tags, widest language coverage. `echocall-multilingual`: balanced multilingual quality. Each model supports a different set of languages for `language`/`supportedLanguages` - pick a model that covers your target language(s), otherwise the request may fail.

speed.description: Speaking speed multiplier (0.7-1.2). 0.9 = slower/clearer, 1.0 = normal, 1.1 = faster.

turnEagerness.description: How quickly the agent responds: patient (waits longer), normal, eager (responds fast).

enableInterruptions.description: If true, the agent will stop speaking immediately when the user starts talking.

enableBackchannel.description: Enables realistic listening sounds like "mhm", "yeah", "I see" during user speech.

enableFillers.description: Allows the agent to use natural filler words like "well", "actually" to sound more human.

backgroundVoiceDetection.description: If true, the agent detects and ignores background noise/voices.

asrKeywords.description: Keywords for improved ASR recognition (product names, brand names, etc.).

saveCallAudio.description: Whether to record and store the full audio of the conversation for later review.

zeroPiiRetention.description: Privacy mode. If enabled, PII data is stripped and logs are not permanently stored.

retentionDays.description: Number of days to keep conversation logs. Defaults to 30. Set to -1 for permanent storage.

systemToolsConfig.description: System tool toggles (endCall, voicemailDetection, languageDetection, playKeypadTouchTone, skipTurn).

transferNumbers.description: Phone numbers the agent can transfer calls to.

body.description: The agent configuration. `systemToolsConfig` switches on the built-in call-control tools, and `transferNumbers` lists the numbers the agent may hand a call over to.

tools.name: get_agent
tools.description:
Get a voice agent

Returns the full public configuration of one voice agent, including the system prompt, the opening line, model settings and the recording and retention settings. Internal voice engine identifiers are never included. A reseller key may read any agent belonging to that reseller; an ordinary key only its own. An identifier that is not a number after the `agent_` prefix is removed is rejected with 400.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description:
Update a voice agent

Changes one or more fields on a voice agent. Every field is optional and only the fields you send are written, so this is a partial update. The change is pushed to the voice engine first and then stored; if the engine rejects the push the request still succeeds and the new values are stored, so a caller that depends on live behaviour should verify the agent afterwards. The response carries the agent id and a confirmation message, not the updated agent.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

supportedLanguages.description: All supported languages as ISO-639-1 codes.

firstMessage.description: Initial message spoken by the agent

ttsModel.description: Text-to-speech model. Leave unset for automatic selection based on `language`. `echocall-flash`: fast, multilingual (recommended default). `echocall-flash-lite`: fastest, English only. `echocall-ultra`: most expressive/natural, supports emotional audio tags, widest language coverage. `echocall-multilingual`: balanced multilingual quality. Each model supports a different set of languages for `language`/`supportedLanguages` - pick a model that covers your target language(s), otherwise the request may fail.

similarityBoost.description: How closely the speech follows the original voice (0.0-1.0). Default: 0.75.

optimizeStreamingLatency.description: Latency optimisation (0-4). Higher answers faster at slightly lower quality. Default: 3.

expressiveMode.description: Expressive speech with audio tags. Takes effect with the echocall-ultra model.

suggestedAudioTags.description: Up to 20 audio tags (for example "happy", "whispers") the agent may use in expressive mode.

enableInterruptions.description: Allow user to interrupt the agent

transferNumbers.description: Phone numbers the agent can transfer calls to.

body.description: The fields to change. Sending an empty object is accepted and touches only the updated timestamp.

tools.name: delete_agent
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete a voice agent

Deletes a voice agent permanently and removes it from the voice engine. This cannot be undone, and any phone number still routed to this agent stops being answered by it. Its integration links and knowledge entries are deleted with it, and so are the indexed knowledge documents that no other agent uses. The removal in the voice engine is attempted first, but a failure there does not stop the local deletion, so the agent always disappears from the account. This endpoint takes no request body.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: list_agent_integrations
tools.description:
List integrations assigned to an agent

Returns every integration currently assigned to this voice agent, together with the tools the agent may call through it. The `enabledTools` field decides which of the integration actions the assistant may call: null means the recommended default set for that integration type, an empty array means the assistant may call nothing, and a list of tool names means exactly those tools and no others. Tool names are the `name` values from the integration tool catalogue. A list may only name tools the permissions of the integration allow (`permitted` in the catalogue, see GET /integrations/{id}/permissions); a tool outside them is refused with 422 and error code `tool_not_permitted`, while a malformed list or an unknown tool name stays a 400 `validation_error`. The response is a plain list with no paging, and it includes the health state of each integration so you can see whether a tool would actually work today. Only integrations of the account that owns the agent are listed, which for a reseller key is the customer account: an assignment that points at an integration of another account is left out.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

tools.name: assign_agent_integration
tools.description:
Assign an integration to an agent

Gives a voice agent access to one integration, so its tools become callable during a call. The integration must belong to the account that owns the agent, which for a reseller key is the customer account, not the reseller. The `enabledTools` field decides which of the integration actions the assistant may call: null means the recommended default set for that integration type, an empty array means the assistant may call nothing, and a list of tool names means exactly those tools and no others. Tool names are the `name` values from the integration tool catalogue. A list may only name tools the permissions of the integration allow (`permitted` in the catalogue, see GET /integrations/{id}/permissions); a tool outside them is refused with 422 and error code `tool_not_permitted`, while a malformed list or an unknown tool name stays a 400 `validation_error`. Assigning an integration that is already assigned returns 409. After the row is written the new tool set is pushed to the voice engine; if that push fails the assignment is rolled back and the request returns 502, so the response always reflects the live agent.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

integrationId.description: Identifier of the integration to assign. It must already exist on the account that owns the assistant.

enabledTools.description: Exact tools the assistant may call through this integration. Null selects the recommended default set for the integration type, an empty array disables every tool, and a list selects exactly the named tools.

body.description: The integration to assign, and optionally the tools to enable. Omit `enabledTools` to accept the recommended default set. Only catalogue-backed integration types accept a tool list.

tools.name: update_agent_integration_tools
tools.description:
Change the tool selection for an assigned integration

Replaces the tool selection for one integration already assigned to a voice agent. The `enabledTools` field decides which of the integration actions the assistant may call: null means the recommended default set for that integration type, an empty array means the assistant may call nothing, and a list of tool names means exactly those tools and no others. Tool names are the `name` values from the integration tool catalogue. A list may only name tools the permissions of the integration allow (`permitted` in the catalogue, see GET /integrations/{id}/permissions); a tool outside them is refused with 422 and error code `tool_not_permitted`, while a malformed list or an unknown tool name stays a 400 `validation_error`. The field is required: a body without an `enabledTools` key is rejected with 400, while an explicit null restores the recommended default set. The new selection is saved and then pushed to the voice engine; if the push fails the request returns 502 but the saved selection is kept, so a retry only has to repeat the push. An integration of another account answers 404 as if it were not assigned.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

integrationId.description: Numeric identifier of the integration whose assignment is being changed. This is the integration id, not the assignment id.

enabledTools.description: Exact tools the assistant may call through this integration. Null selects the recommended default set for the integration type, an empty array disables every tool, and a list selects exactly the named tools.

body.description: The complete new tool selection. This replaces the previous selection rather than adding to it.

tools.name: remove_agent_integration
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Remove an integration from an agent

Unassigns an integration from a voice agent, so the agent can no longer call any of its tools. The integration itself is untouched and stays available to assign elsewhere. The reduced tool set is pushed to the voice engine after the row is removed; if that push fails the request returns 502 and the integration is already unassigned locally but may still be callable until a later change syncs. agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

integrationId.description: Numeric identifier of the integration whose assignment is being changed. This is the integration id, not the assignment id.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: list_agent_knowledge
tools.description:
List agent knowledge sources

Returns every knowledge source attached to one voice agent, newest first. These are the documents the agent may draw on when answering, added either as a crawled web page or as literal text. The response is a plain list with no paging. Entries belong to the account that owns the agent, so a reseller key that reads a customer agent sees the same entries as the customer.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

tools.name: add_agent_knowledge
tools.description:
Add a knowledge source to an agent

Adds one knowledge source to a voice agent. The body is one of three shapes chosen by `type`: `url` reads one page and reads it again every `syncInterval` (weekly by default), `text` takes up to 200000 characters of `text` to store verbatim, `crawl` reads a whole website from its start page, up to `maxDepth` links deep and `maxPages` pages, and crawls it again every `syncInterval`. A crawl runs in the background with status `pending`; follow it with `GET /agents/{agentId}/knowledge/crawl`. `title` is optional and defaults to the URL, the host name for a crawl, or to "Text Knowledge" for a text entry. Files go through `POST /agents/{agentId}/knowledge/files`. The document is created in the voice engine and then attached to the agent, which from then on draws on it in calls. The entry is stored under the account that owns the agent, also when a reseller key adds it. When the document cannot be created or attached, the request still succeeds and the entry is stored with status `failed`; delete it and add it again.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

url.description: Web URL to crawl and index as knowledge

title.description: Human-readable title for this knowledge source

syncInterval.description: How often the page is read again. Defaults to weekly, `off` reads it once.

body.description: A page, a text or a website. Set `type` to `url` and send `url`, to `text` and send `text`, or to `crawl` and send the start page as `url`.

tools.name: add_agent_knowledge_file
tools.description:
Add a file to an agent knowledge base

Adds a file as knowledge source to a voice agent, as the dashboard upload does. Send the file as base64 in `base64` with its name in `fileName`. Allowed are PDF, TXT, MD, CSV and JSON files of at most 15 MB; the content must match the extension (a PDF starts with `%PDF-`, text files are UTF-8), otherwise the request is rejected with 400. Over MCP the whole request may be at most 1 MB, so larger files go through the API directly. The document is created in the voice engine and attached to the agent. When that fails, the request still succeeds and the entry is stored with status `failed`; delete it and add it again.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

base64.description: The file content, base64 encoded. At most 15 MB decoded. Over MCP the whole request may be at most 1 MB, so larger files go through the API directly.

title.description: Human-readable title. Defaults to the file name.

body.description: The file and its name.

tools.name: delete_agent_knowledge
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete an agent knowledge source

Removes one knowledge source from a voice agent: the entry is deleted and the agent no longer draws on the document. The indexed document is deleted from the voice engine as well, unless another entry or another agent still uses it. The entry must belong to this agent, otherwise the request is rejected with 404. A failure in the voice engine is logged and does not stop the local deletion. This endpoint takes no request body.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

knowledgeId.description: Identifier of the knowledge entry to remove.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: refresh_agent_knowledge
tools.description:
Refresh an agent knowledge source

Re-reads a URL knowledge source from its source page immediately and replaces the stored content with what the page says now. Website sources are also re-read on a schedule, so this is for the case where a page changed and the agent should know about it at once. Only entries of type `url` can be refreshed; text and file entries are rejected with 400. The entry must belong to this agent and to the account behind the key, otherwise the request is rejected with 404. This endpoint takes no request body.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent. Accepted either as the public form `agent_12` or as the bare number `12`; the prefix is stripped before the lookup.

knowledgeId.description: Identifier of the knowledge entry to refresh.

tools.name: list_chatbots
tools.description:
List chatbots

Returns the chatbots visible to the key, newest first. An ordinary account key sees only its own chatbots; a reseller key sees every chatbot belonging to that reseller and can narrow the result to one customer with `userId`. Paging defaults to 100 items per page, which is also the maximum. `pagination.total` is a real count of every chatbot matching the request, produced by a separate count query, so a page count can be worked out from it.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

userId.description: Reseller keys only: restrict the result to a single customer account. The key must be a reseller key and the account must be one of that reseller customers, otherwise the request is rejected with 403. Ignored for ordinary account keys, which always see only their own records.

tools.name: create_chatbot
tools.description:
Create a chatbot

Creates a chatbot and provisions it in the voice engine in the same request, then derives its hosted chat page URL from the new identifier. Only `name` is required; the language defaults to `de` and the widget appearance fields all have platform defaults. The widget microphone stays off until `enableVoice` is true; a spoken conversation then runs on the voice allowance of the account, and `voiceId` chooses the voice from GET /voices or GET /voices/available. Unset text fields are stored with sensible fallbacks, so an omitted `greeting` becomes a generic opening line and an omitted display name repeats `name`. The response carries the new identifier and the public URL, not the full chatbot.
