Add a knowledge source to a chatbot

Adds one knowledge source to a chatbot. `type` says how to read `content`: for `url` it is the address to draw from, read again every `syncInterval` (weekly by default), for `text` it is the literal text, for `file` it is the text of the file, named by `fileName` and described by `mimeType`, and for `crawl` it is the start page of a website that is read up to `maxDepth` links deep and `maxPages` pages and crawled again every `syncInterval`. A crawl runs in the background with status `pending`; follow it with `GET /chatbots/{chatbotId}/knowledge/crawl`. `content` is always required and must not be empty. The document is created in the voice engine and then attached to the chatbot, which from then on draws on it in conversations. The entry is stored under the account that owns the chatbot, also when a reseller key adds it. When the document cannot be created or attached, the request still succeeds and the entry is stored with status `failed`; delete it and add it again. Note that the 400 response for an invalid body carries only an error code and a `details` list, with no `message` key, unlike the other endpoints.

syncInterval.description: For `url` and `crawl`: how often the page or website is read again. Defaults to weekly, `off` reads it once.

maxDepth.description: For `crawl`: how many links deep the crawl follows from the start page.

maxPages.description: For `crawl`: at most this many pages are read.

body.description: The knowledge source. `title`, `fileName` and `mimeType` are optional and stored as given; without a `title` the entry is named after the URL or the file name.

tools.name: delete_chatbot_knowledge
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete a chatbot knowledge source

Removes one knowledge source from a chatbot: the entry is deleted and the chatbot no longer draws on the document. The indexed document is deleted from the voice engine as well, unless another entry or another agent still uses it. The chatbot must be one the key may use and the entry must belong to this chatbot, otherwise the request is rejected with 404, so a repeated call answers 404. A failure in the voice engine is logged and does not stop the local deletion. This endpoint takes no request body.

knowledgeId.description: Identifier of the knowledge entry to remove.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: refresh_chatbot_knowledge
tools.description:
Refresh a chatbot knowledge source

Re-reads a URL knowledge source from its source page immediately and replaces the stored content with what the page says now. Website sources are also re-read on a schedule, so this is for the case where a page changed and the chatbot should know about it at once. Only entries of type `url` can be refreshed; text and file entries are rejected with 400. The entry must belong to this chatbot and to the account behind the key, otherwise the request is rejected with 404. This endpoint takes no request body.

knowledgeId.description: Identifier of the knowledge entry to refresh.

tools.name: list_phone_numbers
tools.description:
List phone numbers

Returns the phone numbers the account rents, newest purchase first. Wholesale costs, carrier identifiers and SIP credentials are never included, only the columns of the PhoneNumber schema. A reseller key sees every number belonging to its own customers and can narrow the result to one customer with `userId`; a direct account key ignores `userId` and always sees only its own numbers. `pagination.total` is a real count of every number matching the request, not the length of the page, so a page count can be computed from it.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

userId.description: Reseller keys only: restrict the result to one customer account. The customer must belong to the calling reseller, otherwise the request is rejected with 403. Ignored for direct account keys.

tools.name: list_phone_number_countries
tools.description:
List purchasable countries

Returns every country whose numbers can currently be bought through the number marketplace. Use the `iso` field of an entry as the `countryIso` argument of the number search and of a purchase. The list is read live from the marketplace and is not paginated. When the marketplace is not enabled for this deployment the endpoint answers 503 instead of an empty list.

tools.name: search_phone_numbers
tools.description:
Search available numbers

Searches the number marketplace for numbers that can be bought right now in one country. Nothing is reserved: a listing can disappear between the search and the purchase, so buy promptly and be ready to retry with a different result. Each entry carries the prices, the capabilities and the identifiers a purchase needs, and should be passed back to the purchase endpoint unchanged. The marketplace applies its own rate limit; when it is hit the endpoint answers 429 and the search can be repeated after a short pause.

countryIso.description: Two-letter ISO country code to search in, exactly 2 characters. Take it from the `iso` field of the countries endpoint.

numberType.description: Restrict the search to one category of number. Omit to let the marketplace decide which categories to return.

areaCode.description: Area or city code to search within. Only meaningful for number types that have one, such as `local`.

limit.description: Maximum number of listings to return. Must be between 1 and 100; a value outside that range is rejected with 400 rather than clamped.

tools.name: purchase_phone_number
tools.description:
COSTS MONEY: Purchase a phone number

Buys one of the numbers returned by the search and attaches it to the account. Buying numbers needs an active Voice subscription (Voice, Bundle or a voice capable plan) and is not possible during the free trial; otherwise the request is rejected with 403 and one of the codes `voice_subscription_required`, `voice_subscription_inactive` or `trial_not_allowed`, before anything is charged. This charges money: the setup price plus the first month, plus VAT, is deducted from the account wallet, a balance transaction is written and an invoice is issued. An account managed by a provider (a partner of EchoCall) pays the provider's price as the search shows it and gets the invoice from that provider; when the provider cannot take the order right now the request is rejected with 400 `provider_unavailable`, nothing is bought and the provider is informed. Pass the listing from the search result back unchanged.

body.description: The listing to buy, exactly as returned by the search. `availableDidId` and `skuId` identify the listing at the marketplace, `features` lists the capabilities of the number, and `requirementId` names the regulatory requirement set to satisfy, if there is one. The four price fields are deprecated: they are optional, they are ignored, and the server prices the purchase itself. They remain in the schema only so integrations that echo a whole search result back keep working.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: get_phone_number
tools.description:
Get a phone number

Returns one phone number of the account. The response is the PhoneNumber object itself, not wrapped in a `data` envelope. Use it to read the current assignment, the lifecycle status and the regulatory verification state of a number. A number that does not belong to the calling account answers 404 rather than 403.

tools.name: update_phone_number
tools.description:
Update a phone number

Changes which agent answers on a number and the label it carries in the dashboard. Only the fields present in the body are written, everything else is left alone; a body with no known field is rejected with 400. The response is an acknowledgement message only, it does not echo the updated record: read the number back with the GET endpoint if you need the new state. `voiceAgentId` takes the id GET /phone-numbers/assignable-agents returns (`agent_12`) or the bare number. The agent has to be one of the account's own voice agents and ready to take calls, and the number is pointed at it at the phone service in the same step, so calls are answered by it right away. An agent of another account answers 404 `agent_not_found`, an agent that is not set up yet 409 `agent_not_ready`, and when the phone service cannot be reached the answer is 503 `provider_unavailable` and nothing is changed.

voiceAgentId.description: The voice agent that answers this number, as `agent_12` or 12 from GET /phone-numbers/assignable-agents. null frees the number.

body.description: The fields to change. `voiceAgentId` points the number at a voice agent, or clears the routing when null, and `label` sets the display name returned as `friendlyName`.

tools.name: cancel_phone_number
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Cancel a phone number

Cancels a number bought through the marketplace, with a 30 day grace period: the number is released at the carrier straight away but stays usable on the account until `cancelationEndDate`, and the record is kept rather than deleted. Only marketplace numbers can be cancelled here; a number that was imported by other means is rejected with 400. Cancelling twice is rejected with 409. This does not refund the setup charge or the month already paid for.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: get_phone_number_verification
tools.description:
Get the verification requirement

Returns what the regulator demands before this number can carry traffic. When the number needs no verification the response is `{ "kycRequired": false, "requirement": null }`. Otherwise `requirement` describes the accepted identity kinds, how many documents of which type are needed, which fields are mandatory and which forms must be signed. Read this first: it tells you exactly what to put in the submission body.

tools.name: submit_phone_number_verification
tools.description:
Submit verification

Submits the identity, address and document proofs demanded for a regulated number. Upload the document files first and pass their identifiers in `proofs`; which document types are accepted and how many are needed comes from the requirement endpoint. The submission is forwarded to the registry and the number moves to the `pending` verification state, from where the status endpoint reports progress. A number that needs no verification is rejected with 400, and a number already approved or already awaiting review is rejected with 409, so a rejected submission must be corrected and sent again rather than duplicated.

body.description: The verification package. `identityType` picks between a personal and a business identity and decides which of the optional identity fields are mandatory, per the requirement set. `phoneNumberField` is the contact number of the identity, not the number being verified. `countryId` is the registry country identifier and is used for both the identity and the address. `addressLine`, `cityName` and `postalCode` are the registered address. Each entry in `proofs` names an uploaded file, the document type it satisfies and whether it proves the identity or the address.

tools.name: get_phone_number_verification_status
tools.description:
Get verification status

Polls the current state of the regulatory verification for a number. Once a submission exists the state is read live from the registry and the stored value on the number record is updated to match, so this endpoint is what to poll after submitting. Before any submission it answers `not_submitted` for a number that needs verification, and the number's recorded state, normally `not_required`, for one that does not. When the registry rejected the submission, `rejectReasons` says why; it is null in every other case.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description:
List conversations

Returns a page of conversations, newest first. One `type` is listed at a time: `voice` returns call records and `chat` returns widget and WhatsApp threads. A call record carries its length in seconds and `billedMinutes`, the voice minutes it counts (every started minute counts, a call that never connected counts 0). Every item carries a `type` field so a client can tell the two shapes apart without remembering which query it sent. The pagination object reports `page`, `perPage`, the `type` that was listed and `total`, a real count of the conversations of that type on the account.

type.description: Which kind of conversation to list. Any value other than `chat` is treated as `voice`.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description:
Get a conversation

Returns one conversation. The `type` query parameter selects which store the id is looked up in and must match the kind of record you are asking for, since voice calls and chat threads number themselves independently. A voice call is returned on its own. A chat conversation is returned together with its full transcript in `messages`, ordered oldest first and not paginated; for a long thread use the messages endpoint instead. An id that is not a number is rejected with 400, and one that is not found under the selected type answers 404.

id.description: Identifier of the conversation, in the id space of the selected `type`.

type.description: Which kind of conversation the id refers to. Any value other than `chat` is treated as `voice`.

tools.name: update_conversation
tools.description:
Update a chat conversation

Changes the status, the archive flag or the assigned human agent of a chat conversation. Chat threads only: an id belonging to a voice call is rejected with 400, and a body with no updatable field is rejected with 400 as well. Assigning an agent also stamps the assignment time and, unless the same request sets a status, moves the thread to `active`, mirroring what the dashboard does. Setting the status to `closed` runs the same finalisation as the close endpoint, recomputing the conversation analytics. The updated conversation is returned in `data`.

assignedAgentId.description: Live chat agent to assign, or null to unassign.

body.description: The fields to change. `status` moves the thread between `waiting`, `active` and `closed`, `isArchived` moves it in and out of the inbox, and `assignedAgentId` names the human agent to hand it to, or null to unassign. At least one field must be present.

tools.name: list_conversation_messages
tools.description:
List conversation messages

Returns a page of the transcript of a chat conversation, oldest message first, so paging forward follows the conversation in order. This endpoint serves chat threads only: an id that belongs to a voice call is rejected with 400 rather than a misleading 404, and the transcript of a call is carried on the call record itself. Unlike the conversation list, the pagination object here carries a real `total`, counted over the whole transcript.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: send_conversation_message
tools.description:
Reply in a conversation

Sends a message into a chat conversation as a human agent, delivering it to the visitor over the same channel the thread runs on. An API key is not itself an agent session, so the message is attributed to the agent already assigned to the thread, or to the account's first live chat agent when it is unassigned. An account with no live chat agent at all cannot send and is rejected with 409. Chat threads only: a voice call id is rejected with 400. A thread whose state does not allow a reply, a closed one for example, is rejected with 412.

message.description: The text sent to the visitor as a human agent reply.

body.description: The reply text to deliver to the visitor. It may not be empty.

tools.name: close_conversation
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Close a chat conversation

Closes a chat conversation and finalises it: the closing time is stamped and the response time and duration figures of the thread are recomputed, which is what the analytics endpoints then report. Chat threads only, a voice call id is rejected with 400. This endpoint takes no request body. Closing an already closed conversation runs the finalisation again rather than failing. The closed conversation is returned in `data`.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: get_analytics_summary
tools.description:
Get a usage summary

Returns usage over a date window, aggregated into one row per usage type, with the quantity consumed and the revenue, cost and margin that go with it. Rows appear only for usage types that were actually recorded in the window, so an idle account gets an empty `metrics` array rather than rows of zeroes. Both bounds are optional: without them the window is the last 30 days ending now. The window that was actually applied is echoed in `period`.

from.description: Start of the window, inclusive. Defaults to 30 days before now. A date-time value is accepted as well as a date.

to.description: End of the window, inclusive. Defaults to now. A date-time value is accepted as well as a date.

tools.name: get_daily_analytics
tools.description:
Get daily call metrics

Returns one row of metrics per calendar day, oldest day first, ready to plot as a time series. The figures are read live from the conversation records, so a conversation is counted as soon as it has ended, and the voice calls, chat sessions and avatar sessions of the account each count as one call. Cost is in USD, as the voice engine reports it. Days with no activity are absent from the result rather than present as zeroes. The window is the last `days` days counted back from now, optionally narrowed to a single agent. The applied `days` value and `agentId` are echoed in the response, which matters because an out-of-range or non-numeric `days` is silently replaced by 30 rather than rejected.

days.description: Size of the window in days. Must be between 1 and 365; a value outside that range, or one that is not a number, falls back to 30 without an error. Check the `days` field of the response for what was used.

agentId.description: Restrict the series to one voice agent, by its `agent_42` identifier or the bare number. Omit for the whole account. No error is raised for an unknown agent, the series is simply empty.

tools.name: get_agent_analytics
tools.description:
Get agent statistics

Returns the lifetime aggregate metrics of one voice agent: call counts, durations, cost, token consumption and quality scores. The figures are read live from the conversation records, so a call is counted as soon as it has ended. Cost is in USD, as the voice engine reports it. An agent that exists but has no recorded activity yet answers 200 with `stats` set to null. An agent that does not belong to the calling account answers 404, the same as one that does not exist; a path segment that is not a number answers 400.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent, as `agent_42` or the bare number.

tools.name: get_chatbot_analytics
tools.description:
Get chatbot statistics

Returns the lifetime aggregate metrics of one chatbot: session counts, durations, cost, token consumption and quality scores. The figures are read live from the conversation records and count a chat session and a spoken widget conversation alike, so the fields are named after calls even though most entries are chat sessions; the two call-length extremes tracked for voice agents are absent. Cost is in USD, as the voice engine reports it. A chatbot with no recorded activity yet answers 200 with `stats` set to null. A chatbot that does not belong to the calling account answers 404, the same as one that does not exist; a path segment that is not a number answers 400.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description:
List your webhook endpoints

Returns every outbound webhook endpoint registered by the account, newest first and unpaged. The signing secret is not part of this response and cannot be read back at any point: it is shown once, when the endpoint is created. Use `failedDeliveries`, `lastDeliveryAt` and `lastDeliveryStatus` to spot an endpoint that has started rejecting deliveries before it is switched off automatically.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description:
Register a webhook endpoint

Registers an HTTPS endpoint and subscribes it to the named events. The response contains a `secret`, and this is the only time it is ever returned: store it before you do anything else, because no endpoint anywhere in this API will show it to you again, and losing it means deleting the endpoint and registering a new one. The secret keys the HMAC-SHA256 signature sent with every delivery in the `X-EchoCall-Signature` header, which is how you prove a payload really came from us. Every name in `events` must be a name from GET /webhooks/events, or the literal `*` for all of them; an unknown name is rejected with 400 rather than silently never firing. The target URL is resolved and refused with 400 if it points at a private or internal address.

body.description: The destination URL, which must be publicly resolvable, and at least one event name to subscribe to.

tools.name: list_webhook_events
tools.description:
List the events you can subscribe to

Returns the catalogue of outbound events with a one-line explanation of when each is emitted. These names, plus the wildcard returned in `wildcard`, are the only values accepted in the `events` list when creating or updating an endpoint. `webhook.test` appears in the catalogue but is never produced by platform activity: it is only sent when you ask for a test delivery.

tools.name: get_webhook
tools.description:
Read one webhook endpoint

Returns a single registered endpoint, wrapped in a `data` object. The signing secret is not included and cannot be recovered here or anywhere else. Note `isActive` together with `failedDeliveries`: an endpoint is disabled automatically once 25 consecutive deliveries have failed, and a single successful delivery resets that counter to zero.

id.description: Identifier of the endpoint. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: update_webhook
tools.description:
Update a webhook endpoint

Changes the destination URL, the subscription list or the enabled flag of an endpoint. Every field is optional and only the fields you send are touched. `events` is replaced wholesale, not merged, so send the complete list you want; each name is checked against the catalogue and an unknown one fails the whole request with 400. A new URL is resolved and refused if it points at a private or internal address. Setting `isActive` back to true is how you bring back an endpoint that was disabled automatically after repeated failures. The signing secret is not changed and cannot be rotated through this endpoint.

body.description: The fields to change. `events`, if sent, replaces the existing subscription list entirely.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete a webhook endpoint

Removes an endpoint permanently. Deliveries stop at once and the signing secret is destroyed with the record, so this cannot be undone: registering the same URL again produces a new endpoint with a new secret. If you only want to pause deliveries, set `isActive` to false with a PATCH instead.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description:
Send a test delivery

Sends one signed `webhook.test` payload to the endpoint and reports what happened, synchronously and with no retry. This is a real delivery: it is signed with the endpoint's secret, so it is the right way to check your signature verification. It updates `lastDeliveryAt` and `lastDeliveryStatus` and nothing else: a failed test never counts towards the automatic disabling that follows 25 consecutive real failures, and a successful one neither resets `failedDeliveries` nor re-enables an endpoint you disabled yourself. A transport failure is reported inside a 200 response with `delivered` false, not as an HTTP error.

id.description: Identifier of the endpoint to ping.

tools.name: list_tickets
tools.description:
List support tickets

Returns the account's support tickets, newest first, with no paging. By default only open work is listed: tickets in state `closed` or `resolved` are left out unless you ask for them. Pass `includeArchived=true` to get exactly the closed and resolved ones instead, or `status` to filter to a single state. `includeArchived` takes precedence over `status` when both are sent. Neither parameter is validated against a fixed list, so a misspelled `status` is not an error, it simply matches no tickets and returns an empty array.

status.description: Return only tickets in this state. The states in use are `open`, `in_progress`, `waiting`, `resolved` and `closed`. Not validated: an unrecognised value matches nothing. Ignored when `includeArchived=true` is also sent.

includeArchived.description: Set to `true` to list the archive, meaning exactly the `closed` and `resolved` tickets, instead of the open ones. Only the literal string `true` has any effect; every other value, including `false`, leaves the default behaviour in place.

tools.name: create_ticket
tools.description:
Open a support ticket

Creates a support ticket on behalf of the authenticated account and returns its identifier. The ticket starts in state `open`, and `category` and `priority` fall back to `other` and `medium` when they are not given. Put everything a human needs into `description`: error messages, the identifiers involved and the steps that led to the problem, since the first reply is written by a person reading exactly this text. Creating a ticket also emits the `ticket.created` outbound webhook event to any endpoint subscribed to it.

subject.description: A concise summary of the issue or request.

description.description: Full details of the support request. Use this to provide context, error messages, or steps to reproduce.

category.description: The functional area this ticket relates to.

priority.description: The urgency level. Urgent tickets are prioritized for immediate reseller/admin attention.

body.description: The subject line and the full description, plus the optional `category` and `priority`. `category` groups the ticket by functional area and `priority` sets how urgently it is picked up.

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.description:
Read a ticket and its thread

Returns one ticket with its full public message thread, oldest message first. Internal notes written by staff for staff are filtered out and never appear here, so the thread you see is the correspondence you took part in. Each message carries the sender's display name and role. `System` is used where a message was generated by the platform rather than typed by a person; a person who has no name on record reports `null`, so render your own label for them rather than a placeholder. A ticket belonging to another account answers 404 rather than 403.

ticketId.description: Ticket identifier. Accepted with or without the `ticket_` prefix: both `ticket_42` and `42` address the same ticket.

tools.name: reply_to_ticket
tools.description:
Reply to a ticket

Adds a public reply to an existing ticket and bumps its last-changed timestamp, which is what moves the ticket back up the support queue. A ticket in state `closed` cannot be replied to and returns 400; a resolved ticket still accepts replies, so use this to reopen a conversation that was closed too early. Attachments are referenced by URL, they are not uploaded here: host the file somewhere the support team can reach and pass the link. The reply emits the `ticket.updated` outbound webhook event.

ticketId.description: Ticket identifier, with or without the `ticket_` prefix.

message.description: The content of your reply or update.

filename.description: The name of the uploaded file.

url.description: The public URL where the attachment is hosted.

mimeType.description: The logical file type (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).

attachments.description: Optional list of file attachments supporting the message.

body.description: The reply text and, optionally, a list of attachments. Each attachment describes an already-hosted file: its name, a URL the support team can download it from, its content type and its size in bytes.

tools.name: list_bookings
tools.description:
List the bookings in your connected calendars

Returns the bookings of every active integration that has a calendar (Cal.com, Calendly, Google Calendar, Outlook), sorted by start, or of one integration when you pass `integrationId`. Each booking carries the `id` that the confirm, decline and cancel paths take. Bookings are read live from the calendar provider on every request, so poll at a calm pace (once a minute is plenty) rather than in a tight loop. Each calendar is read across every page its provider hands out, up to a fixed limit, and over a fixed window: Cal.com and Calendly from 3 months back, Google Calendar and Outlook from now, each up to 12 months ahead. `from` and `to` only narrow that window, so a range outside it comes back empty without the calendar being listed in `failed`. A calendar that could not be read in full this time is listed in `failed`. When it could not be read at all, none of its bookings are in `data`. When it was read only in part (a later page failed, or it holds more bookings than the limit), the bookings that were read are in `data` and the rest are missing.

status.description: Only bookings in these states, as a comma separated list of `accepted`, `pending`, `cancelled` and `rejected`. Case does not matter.

from.description: Only bookings that start at or after this moment. ISO 8601 with time and offset. It narrows the window each calendar is read over and does not widen it.

to.description: Only bookings that start at or before this moment. ISO 8601 with time and offset. Must not be earlier than `from`.

tools.name: list_integration_event_types
tools.description:
List the event types of a calendar integration

Returns the kinds of appointment that can be booked through this integration, read live from the calendar provider: their name, their duration in minutes and their identifier. An empty list means the calendar has no event types; a provider that cannot be reached or refuses is answered with 502 `provider_error`, not with an empty list.

tools.name: confirm_booking
tools.description:
Confirm a booking request

Confirms a booking that waits for the host (status `pending`). The calendar provider then informs the attendee as it always does. Only calendars with booking requests support this (Cal.com). The others answer 422 `not_supported`.

bookingId.description: The `id` of the booking as GET /integrations/bookings returns it.

tools.name: decline_booking
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Decline a booking request

Declines a booking that waits for the host (status `pending`). The optional `reason` is handed to the calendar provider, which may show it to the attendee. Only calendars with booking requests support this (Cal.com). The others answer 422 `not_supported`.

bookingId.description: The `id` of the booking as GET /integrations/bookings returns it.

body.description: Optional `reason`, at most 500 characters. An empty object or no body declines without a reason.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: cancel_booking
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Cancel a booking

Cancels a booking in the calendar of the integration. The optional `reason` is handed to the calendar provider, which may show it to the attendee.

bookingId.description: The `id` of the booking as GET /integrations/bookings returns it.

body.description: Optional `reason`, at most 500 characters. An empty object or no body cancels without a reason.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: list_integration_types
tools.description:
List the integration types you can connect

Returns the catalogue of supported third-party services, each with the configuration fields it needs. Read this before creating an integration: `type` gives you the value to send, and `configFields` tells you exactly which keys belong inside the `config` JSON string and which of them are required. Fields declared with type `password` are masked when the integration is read back, and so is every other key that looks like a secret (see GET /integrations/{id}). The response is a bare JSON array and is the same for every account.

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description:
List your integrations

Returns the account's connected integrations, newest first, as a bare JSON array with no paging. Stored configuration is deliberately left out of the list view: read a single integration to see which of its fields are set. A reseller key may pass `userId` to list one of its own customers' integrations instead; asking for a user who is not a customer of that reseller is refused with 403. On a key that is not a reseller key, `userId` is accepted but has no effect and the caller's own integrations are returned.

userId.description: Reseller keys only: list the integrations of this customer instead of your own. The user must be one of your customers, otherwise the request is refused with 403. Ignored on non-reseller keys.

tools.name: create_integration
tools.description:
Connect an integration

Stores the credentials and settings for one third-party service and returns the new integration's identifier. The integration is created active, but connecting it does not by itself let an agent use it: it still has to be assigned to an agent or chatbot. `config` is a JSON string, not a nested object, so serialise it before sending; the keys it must contain are the ones listed under `configFields` for this type in GET /integrations/types. A `config` that contains the mask `********` anywhere is refused with 400 and error code `masked_without_stored_value`: the mask stands for a stored secret, and a new integration has none, so send the real values. Keys inside `config` that only the server writes (the connection keys and `toolPermissions`) are dropped before the integration is stored. Nothing is contacted at creation time, so a wrong credential is only noticed later: call the test endpoint afterwards to confirm the connection works. A WhatsApp integration whose phone number is already connected in an active integration of another account is refused with 409 and error code `conflict`. A Genesys Cloud integration (type `genesys_cloud`) follows its own rules.

body.description: The service to connect, a name to recognise it by, an optional description, and `config`: a JSON string holding the fields that type requires.

tools.name: get_integration
tools.description:
Read one integration

Returns a single integration including its stored `config`, with every secret value replaced by `********`. A value counts as secret when its field is declared with type `password` for the integration type, when its key contains `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `token`, `apiKey`, `api_key`, `authorization`, `authValue`, `credential`, `bearer` or `cookie` or ends in `Key` (case-insensitive, at any depth), or when it is a URL that carries its secret inside it, such as the webhook URL of a Discord integration. A secret key covers everything below it. Booleans are never masked, and an empty value stays empty. That masking is one-way: this endpoint tells you which credential fields are populated, never what they contain, and there is no endpoint that reveals them. The masked config can be sent back unchanged with PATCH: a secret sent as `********` keeps its stored value. `config` comes back as a JSON string and has to be parsed. Internal connector and health bookkeeping is not returned, and neither are the connection keys only the server writes into `config`.

id.description: Identifier of the integration. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: update_integration
tools.description:
Update an integration

Changes the name, description, stored configuration or enabled flag of an integration. Only the fields you send are written. A `config` you send is merged with the stored one, one object level at a time. A field that is not secret takes the value you send, and one you leave out is removed, so send every non-secret field you want to keep. A secret field keeps its stored value when you leave it out or send it as `********`, an empty string or null clears it, and any other value replaces it. A value counts as secret when its field is declared with type `password` for the integration type, when its key contains `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `token`, `apiKey`, `api_key`, `authorization`, `authValue`, `credential`, `bearer` or `cookie` or ends in `Key` (case-insensitive, at any depth), or when it is a URL that carries its secret inside it, such as the webhook URL of a Discord integration. A secret key covers everything below it. Booleans are never masked, and an empty value stays empty. Nested objects are merged by the same rules.

body.description: The fields to change. `config`, if sent, is merged with the stored configuration: fields that are not secret are replaced, secret fields left out or sent as `********` keep their stored value.

tools.name: delete_integration
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete an integration

Removes the integration and the credentials stored with it. When an account of the service was connected through the dashboard for this integration, that connection is removed as well, unless another integration still uses it; this happens on a best-effort basis and never blocks the delete. This cannot be undone, and any agent that was assigned this integration loses the ability to perform its actions from the moment of deletion: its assignments to agents and chatbots are removed and their tool lists rebuilt at once. To stop use of an integration temporarily while keeping its configuration, set `isActive` to false with a PATCH instead. Deleting a Genesys Cloud integration also ends its running calls, a call can take up to a minute to end, and its access data stop working at once.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: list_integration_tools
tools.description:
List the tools an integration offers

Returns the actions an agent can be allowed to perform through this integration, plus the recommended default selection in `recommended`. Only a few integration types are catalogue-backed; the rest have a fixed tool set that cannot be picked from and answer 404 here, with the same status used for an integration that does not exist or belongs to someone else. Note each tool's `access` level before enabling it: `write` and `delete` tools let the agent change or remove data in the connected service. `permitted` says whether the permissions of the integration (GET /integrations/{id}/permissions) allow agents to use the tool; a tool that is not permitted cannot be put into `enabledTools` of an agent or chatbot.

id.description: Identifier of the integration. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: get_integration_permissions
tools.description:
Read the tool permissions of an integration

Returns which tools the agents of the account may use through this integration: the stored choice in `preset`, every tool of the integration with `allowed`, and how many tools each preset would allow. The permissions limit agents only; the account owner keeps full access through the dashboard and the calendar endpoints. Only Genesys Cloud and the integration types connected through the dashboard sign-in have tool permissions; every other type answers 404, with the same status used for an integration that does not exist or belongs to someone else. `preset` is `legacy` while nothing was chosen: agents then keep the tools they had before permissions existed. A Genesys Cloud integration never reports `legacy`: without a stored choice it reports `read`, which allows only the tools that read. Handing a conversation over to a person is always allowed and is not listed in `tools`.

id.description: Identifier of the integration. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: set_integration_permissions
tools.description:
Set the tool permissions of an integration

Stores which tools the agents of the account may use through this integration, exactly as the dashboard does. Choose a preset (`read`, `read_write`, `full`) or `custom` with the exact tool keys from `tools[].key` of the GET of this path. Only the permissions change; the rest of the stored configuration stays as it is. Every agent and chatbot the integration is assigned to then gets its tool list rebuilt, so the change takes effect in their next conversation: `agentsResynced` counts the agents that were updated, `agentsFailed` the ones that could not be updated now (the saved permissions still apply to them). A tool selection of an agent (`enabledTools`) that names a tool outside the new permissions is not changed, but the tool stays unavailable to the agent. An unusable choice is refused with 422 and error code `validation_error`. Integration types without tool permissions answer 404.

id.description: Identifier of the integration. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

preset.description: `read` allows the reading tools, `read_write` adds the writing tools, `full` allows every tool, `custom` allows exactly the tools listed in `tools`.

tools.description: The tool keys agents may use, as listed under `tools[].key` by GET /integrations/{id}/permissions. Required and non-empty for `custom`, ignored otherwise.

body.description: The new choice: a preset, or `custom` with the exact tool keys agents may use.

tools.name: test_integration
tools.description:
Test an integration

Calls the connected service with the stored credentials and reports what came back. Use it after creating or reconfiguring an integration, since nothing is verified at write time. The shape of the result depends on the integration type: each connector builds its own diagnostic payload, so read it as free-form JSON rather than a fixed schema, and expect at least an indication of success and a message when it failed. Anything resembling a credential is stripped from the result before it is returned. A connection that fails is still reported inside a 200 response, not as an HTTP error. For Genesys Cloud the result has a fixed shape. Without generated access data the test fails and carries no `data`.

id.description: Identifier of the integration to test.

tools.name: get_my_account
tools.description:
Get the current account profile

Returns the account that the presented API key belongs to, which is the simplest way to confirm a key is valid and to discover the user id every other endpoint scopes to. `resellerId` is set when this account is a customer of a reseller, and `ownResellerId` is set when the account operates a reseller itself; both are null for a plain direct account. `avatarUrl` is always null: no avatar image is stored for API consumers, and the field exists only so the shape stays stable. `billingAddress` is the address on your invoices as `PUT /users/me/billing-address` saves it, null while none is saved. The profile is returned as a bare object, not wrapped in a `data` envelope.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.description:
Change your profile name

Changes the name of your account, the `name` that `get_my_account` returns. It applies at once and can be changed back the same way. Only the name changes here: the email address can only be changed by support (ask with `create_ticket`), the invoice address is set with `set_billing_address`. Only the account owner can call this; a team member gets 403.

body.description: The request fields as one JSON object.

tools.name: get_my_usage
tools.description:
Get consumption for a date window

Sums the metered consumption recorded for this account over a date window, broken down into voice minutes and chat sessions. With no query parameters the window runs from midnight on the first day of the current month in server local time up to the moment of the request, which makes the bare call a current-month total. Both bounds are inclusive. The two counters are returned as 0 when nothing was metered in the window rather than being omitted, and the echoed `period` tells you exactly which window was measured. This reports usage only; for what is left to spend, call GET /users/me/limits.

from.description: Start of the window, inclusive. Defaults to the first day of the current month. Parsed as a date; an unparseable value yields an empty result rather than an error.

to.description: End of the window, inclusive. Defaults to the current server time.

tools.name: get_my_limits
tools.description:
Get plan allowances and remaining credit

Returns what the account still has available: its status, its prepaid wallet balance in EUR, the voice minutes and chat conversations left, and the subscribed plan with its monthly allowances. `plan` is null when the account is on no plan, in which case the remaining counters are whatever credit has been granted directly. Poll this before starting a batch of calls or a campaign to avoid running an account to zero mid-run. The answer is a bare object, not wrapped in a `data` envelope.

tools.name: list_languages
tools.description:
List available interface locales

Returns the user interface locales the platform ships, for populating a language picker or for validating a value before writing it to a profile or an agent. The list is read from the locale directories on disk, so it reflects the running build rather than a database table; reseller-specific locale folders are excluded, and so are right to left locales such as Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu, because the interface does not mirror its layout yet. Locales the platform offers only on request are left out as well, the same way the dashboard's language switcher leaves them out. If that directory cannot be read the handler falls back to `en` and `de` instead of failing. Note two things about the shape: the response is a bare JSON array, not the usual `{ data: [...] }` envelope, and each entry carries only a `code`, with no display name. The route requires a valid API key but checks no scope.

tools.name: list_agent_languages
tools.description:
List the languages an agent can speak or write

Returns the languages you can assign to an agent, each with an English name, the name the language calls itself, and a region code for a flag image, so a language picker needs no table of its own. This is a different list from `GET /languages`, which returns the locales the dashboard interface is translated into. Populating an agent picker from the locale list is a common mistake and leaves a customer with three choices where the platform supports dozens. Set `type` to `chat` for a text agent, which has no speech synthesis and therefore the longer list. For `voice`, language support depends on the speech model, so pass the same `ttsModel` value you will create the agent with and the answer matches what that agent will accept; leaving it unset answers for the default model. The voice list is read from the live model catalogue, and `meta.source` reports `catalog` when it came from there or `defaults` when a built-in list was used instead. Set `type` to `all` to name any language code the platform may have stored, which is what a list of agents needs to print a language instead of a bare code.

type.description: Which kind of agent the languages are for, or `all` to name every language the platform knows.

ttsModel.description: Speech model the voice agent will use, for example `echocall-ultra`. Ignored for `type=chat` and `type=all`. Unset means the default model.

tools.name: list_notifications
tools.description:
List account notifications

Returns the notification inbox of the account behind the API key, newest first by creation time. Notifications are raised by the platform for events such as ticket replies or billing changes, and each entry may point at the resource that caused it through `relatedType` and `relatedId`. Pass `unreadOnly=true` to see only unread entries: the handler compares the raw query string against the literal text `true`, so any other value, including `1` or `TRUE`, is treated as not set. The `pagination` object carries `page`, `perPage` and `total`, the last being a real count of the notifications matching the same `unreadOnly` filter as the page.

unreadOnly.description: Set to the literal string `true` to return only unread notifications. Any other value is ignored and the full inbox is returned.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: mark_notification_read
tools.description:
Mark one notification as read

Marks a single notification as read and stamps its `readAt` with the current server time. Ownership is verified first: a notification belonging to another account answers 404 exactly as an unknown id does, so the endpoint never reveals that a foreign id exists. Calling it again on an already read notification succeeds and refreshes `readAt`. This endpoint takes no request body. It answers with a short confirmation message rather than the updated notification.

id.description: Identifier of the notification to mark as read. Must be an integer; a non-numeric value answers 400.

tools.name: mark_all_notifications_read
tools.description:
Mark every notification as read

Marks every unread notification of this account as read in one statement and stamps each with the current server time. Entries that are already read are left untouched, so their original `readAt` is preserved. The call succeeds even when there is nothing unread, and it does not report how many rows it touched. This endpoint takes no request body.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description:
List the account voices

Returns the voices stored on this account, including cloned and generated ones, with the status that tells you whether a voice is ready to be assigned to an agent. The identifier is the platform form `voice_<number>`, which is what agent endpoints on this account expect. The response is not paginated and takes no query parameters: the full set is returned in one call, in insertion order. Access is governed by the `read:agents` scope rather than a voice-specific scope, because voices are only useful in the context of an agent.

tools.name: list_available_voices
tools.description:
List selectable library voices

Returns the voices from the shared library that an agent can be pointed at, each with descriptive labels and the address of a spoken sample. Without `language` the whole library is returned, which is what a portal serving several countries needs; pass a language code to narrow it to the voices offered for that language, plus the account's own cloned and generated voices, which are returned whatever the filter says. Identifiers here are the library ids used when setting a voice on an agent, which differ in form from the `voice_<number>` ids of GET /voices. The response is not paginated, and access is governed by the `read:agents` scope rather than a voice-specific one. If the platform has no voice engine credential configured the call answers 500 with the code `config_error`.

language.description: Narrow the list to voices offered for this language, as a code from GET /languages/agent, for example `de` or `pt-br`. Omit it for the full library.

tools.name: list_plans
tools.description:
List the plans you can subscribe to

Returns the billing plans on offer to the authenticated account. The list is picked for you: an account that belongs to a reseller sees only that reseller's plans, and a direct account sees only the platform's own plans. There is no way to ask for the other set, and attempting to check out a plan from the wrong set is refused with 403. The response is a bare JSON array, not a `{ data: [...] }` envelope, and it is not paged.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description:
List your invoices

Returns the invoices raised against the account, newest first. Without paging the body is a bare JSON array rather than a `{ data: [...] }` envelope, and the whole history comes back on each call; send `page` or `perPage` and the response becomes `{ data, pagination }` with a real `total`. There is no date filter either way. The list holds both kinds of invoice the account can have: ours, for what it paid us, and those of its reseller, for what it paid a reseller that bills its customers itself. Each row says which in `source`. The two kinds are numbered independently, so pass `source` on to GET /billing/invoices/{id}/pdf. An invoice from a reseller appears once the reseller has issued it; its `pdfUrl` is always null and the document is rendered on demand through that endpoint.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: get_subscription
tools.description:
Get the active subscription

Returns the account's current active subscription together with the plan it pays for. Only subscriptions in state `active` are considered; if several exist the most recently created one is returned. An account with no active subscription is not an empty response but a 404, so treat that status as "on no plan" rather than as an error worth retrying.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description:
Get the prepaid balance and remaining allowances

Returns the account's wallet balance in EUR alongside the voice minutes and chat conversations still available in the current period. These are live counters: they fall as calls and conversations are consumed and are topped back up by a plan renewal or an add-on purchase. Use this before starting a batch campaign to confirm there is enough left to pay for it.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.description:
List wallet transactions

Returns movements on the prepaid wallet, newest first: top-ups, charges and manual adjustments, each with the balance that resulted. The `pagination` block echoes the `page` and `perPage` that were used and carries `total`, a real count of the movements on the wallet, so the number of pages can be worked out before fetching them.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: list_addons
tools.description:
List purchasable add-on packages

Returns the add-on packages the account may buy on top of its plan, for example extra voice minutes or extra chat conversations. Only packages that are both active and visible are listed, and, as with plans, a reseller customer sees that reseller's packages while a direct customer sees the platform's own. The order is the catalogue sort order chosen by whoever maintains the packages, not price or name. The response has a `data` array and no pagination block.

tools.name: list_call_campaigns
tools.description:
List batch calling campaigns

Returns the account's outbound campaigns, newest first. Query parameters are validated strictly: an unrecognised `status`, or a `perPage` above 100, is rejected with 400 rather than quietly clamped, which is different from the paging behaviour elsewhere in this API. The `pagination` block echoes the applied page and page size and carries `total`, a real count of the campaigns matching the same `status` filter as the page. Reading campaigns uses the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

page.description: Page to return, starting at 1. Defaults to 1. A value below 1 is rejected with 400, not clamped.

perPage.description: Items per page, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 20. A value outside that range is rejected with 400, not clamped.

status.description: Return only campaigns in this state. Any other value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: create_call_campaign
tools.description:
Create a batch calling campaign

Creates an outbound campaign: a named list of up to 10000 numbers that one voice agent will call. The campaign is created in state `draft` and nothing is dialled until you submit it, so this call places no calls and incurs no call charges. The agent must belong to you, and so must `callerPhoneNumberId` if you set one; either being unknown or owned by someone else gives 404. Per-recipient `metadata` is handed to the agent as conversation context, which is how you personalise each call. This operation is guarded by the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

agentId.description: Identifier of the voice agent to call with, as returned by GET /agents (agent_42)

metadata.description: Custom key-value data passed to the agent as context

scheduledTime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. If omitted, calls start immediately upon submission.

callerPhoneNumberId.description: Database ID of the phone number to call from. If omitted, system default is used.

body.description: The campaign name, the identifier of the voice agent that will place the calls (`agent_42`, as returned by GET /agents), and the recipient list. Optionally `scheduledTime`, an ISO 8601 timestamp for when calls should begin, and `callerPhoneNumberId`, the database id of the number to call from; without it the system default number is used.

tools.name: get_call_campaign
tools.description:
Read a batch calling campaign

Returns one campaign with its current counters: how many numbers it holds and how many calls have succeeded, failed or are still waiting. `batchId` stays null until the campaign is submitted. The counters are the ones stored on the campaign record and are updated as call results arrive, so poll this endpoint to follow a running campaign. It is guarded by the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

campaignId.description: Identifier of the campaign. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

tools.name: delete_call_campaign
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Delete a batch calling campaign

Deletes a campaign and its recipient rows permanently. Only a campaign that was never submitted, or one that has since been cancelled or failed, can be deleted: a submitted campaign in any other state is refused with 409 and has to be cancelled first. Deleting removes the recipient history along with the campaign, so export anything you need from the recipients endpoint before calling this. The response is a bare confirmation message with no `success` field, and the operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: start_call_campaign
tools.description:
COSTS MONEY: Submit a campaign and start calling

Hands a draft campaign to the calling infrastructure and starts it. This is the point where calls are actually placed and charged, so treat it as the irreversible step: only a campaign in state `draft` can be submitted, and submitting one in any other state is refused with 409. A campaign whose recipient list turned out to be empty is refused with 400. If the campaign carries a scheduled time it moves to `scheduled` and dialling begins then, otherwise it moves to `pending` and begins immediately; the state may come straight back as `running` or `completed` if dispatch reports that far already. Outbound calling being unconfigured on the platform gives 503, and a dispatch that returned no batch identifier gives 502. This operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

campaignId.description: Identifier of the draft campaign to submit.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: cancel_call_campaign
tools.description:
IRREVERSIBLE: Cancel a running or scheduled campaign

Stops a submitted campaign: pending calls are abandoned and the campaign moves to `cancelled`. Calls already placed are not undone and remain chargeable, so cancelling limits further spend rather than reversing it. A campaign that was never submitted is refused with 400 and should be deleted instead, and one that is already `completed`, `cancelled` or `failed` is refused with 409. Cancellation is recorded locally even when the upstream stop could not be attempted. This operation uses the `write:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

campaignId.description: Identifier of the campaign to cancel.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call. EchoCall then answers with a confirmation value. Ask the user for a clear yes, then repeat the call with the same arguments and this value.

tools.name: list_call_campaign_recipients
tools.description:
List a campaign's recipients and call results

Returns the numbers in a campaign together with the outcome of each call: status, duration, cost and the identifier of the conversation it produced, where there is one. Rows come back in storage order, which is the order they were supplied in, and the campaign's own state is repeated in `campaignStatus` so a poller does not need a second request. Paging defaults to 50 per page here rather than 20, and `perPage` is clamped to 100. The `pagination` block carries `total`, a count of the recipients stored for this campaign. This operation uses the `read:agents` scope rather than a scope of its own.

campaignId.description: Identifier of the campaign. A non-numeric value is rejected with 400.

page.description: Page to return. Starts at 1; values below 1 are clamped to 1.

perPage.description: Items per page. Clamped to the range 1 to 100; larger values are reduced to 100.

tools.name: list_voice_models
tools.description:
List voice models

The voice models an agent can speak with, as the model picker in the dashboard shows them. Pass `id` as `ttsModel` when you create or update an agent.

tools.name: list_agent_knowledge_crawls
tools.description:
Website crawls of a voice agent

Every website crawl of one voice agent with its progress: pages found, read and failed. A running crawl is checked live, so polling this shows movement. Start a crawl by adding knowledge with `type` `crawl`. Only voice agents of your own account.

agentId.description: agentId

tools.name: cancel_agent_knowledge_crawl
tools.description:
Stop a website crawl of a voice agent

Stops a running crawl. Pages read so far stay in the knowledge entry. Only voice agents of your own account.

agentId.description: agentId

body.description: The request fields as one JSON object.

tools.name: list_agent_knowledge_sync
tools.description:
Auto-sync of a voice agent's website knowledge

For every page and website source of one voice agent: whether and how often it is read again, when it was last updated and whether it can be read again right now. Only voice agents of your own account.

agentId.description: agentId

tools.name: list_chatbot_knowledge_crawls
tools.description:
Website crawls of a chatbot

Every website crawl of one chatbot with its progress: pages found, read and failed. A running crawl is checked live, so polling this shows movement. Start a crawl by adding knowledge with `type` `crawl`. Only chatbots of your own account.

tools.name: cancel_chatbot_knowledge_crawl
tools.description:
Stop a website crawl of a chatbot

Stops a running crawl. Pages read so far stay in the knowledge entry. Only chatbots of your own account.

body.description: The request fields as one JSON object.

tools.name: list_chatbot_knowledge_sync
tools.description:
Auto-sync of a chatbot's website knowledge

For every page and website source of one chatbot: whether and how often it is read again, when it was last updated and whether it can be read again right now. Only chatbots of your own account.

tools.name: get_chatbot_embed_code
tools.description:
Get the embed code of a chatbot

The code that puts the chatbot on a website, as the dashboard offers it: `scriptCode` adds a floating chat button before `</body>`, `iframeCode` places the chat inside a container, `publicUrl` is a direct link to the chat. Only chatbots of your own account.

tools.name: list_chatbot_disclosure_snippets
tools.description:
AI disclosure sentences

Ready-made sentences that tell visitors they are talking to an AI, keyed by language code. The dashboard offers them to insert into a chatbot greeting; using one is optional and the text can be changed freely.

tools.name: get_agent_call_summary
tools.description:
Read the call summary settings of a voice agent

Whether the agent emails a short summary after every call (who called, what about, how urgent, callback number), where it goes, the important numbers and, for each number of the agent, the codes that forward a mobile phone to it when busy, not answered or unreachable. Only agents of your own account.

agentId.description: agentId

tools.name: update_agent_call_summary
tools.description:
Change the call summary of a voice agent

Switches the summary email after every call on or off and sets where it goes, whether it leaves out name and number (`anonymous`) and the important numbers. Fields left out keep their value. Only calls that start after switching on get a summary, usually within five minutes after the call. 409 with `details.reason` `ZERO_PII` when the agent keeps no call data, 400 with `details.reason` `INVALID_VIP` and `details.index` for a number that is not a phone number. Only agents of your own account.

agentId.description: agentId

number.description: National (`0171 1234567`, read as German) or international (`+49 171 1234567`).

vipNumbers.description: Replaces the whole list. Up to 50.

body.description: The request fields as one JSON object.

tools.name: get_chatbot_settings
tools.description:
Get every chatbot setting

Everything the chatbot editor in the dashboard shows, in the shape `PATCH /chatbots/{chatbotId}/settings` takes. Logos come as URLs here and are sent as base64 image data to change them. Only chatbots of your own account.

tools.name: update_chatbot_settings
tools.description:
Update every chatbot setting
